chunks: Even if We send down the angels to them, and the dead should speak to them, and We gather all things before their eyes, they will not believe, unless God should will, for most of them are ignorant.
ai.seo_question: Why do disbelievers not believe even when shown clear signs?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of *Taqdir* (divine decree) regarding faith, illustrating that stubborn disbelievers (*Jahilun*) remain impervious to external proofs like the descent of angels or the speech of the dead. It highlights that true belief requires divine will (*Masha'Allah*) and the removal of spiritual veils, rather than mere accumulation of signs. This aligns with the Imami understanding that guidance is ultimately a gift from God, contingent upon His mercy and the individual's receptivity.
